title: Warehouse transfer
summary: move a quantity of one item from a source warehouse to a destination warehouse, both in the same logistic company, using a manually created warehousing order — and verify that on-hand at the source dropped and on-hand at the destination rose by the same quantity.

phases.title: Confirm stock, destination, and expected order type

tokens.v: Nothing yet. Reading inventory does not change with the transaction type, only what happens to the order does, and a transfer is proved at both ends, so both starting figures are needed. The expected order type comes from the origin and transaction-type combination in Default Order Types by Origin, and its warehousing procedure is what will decide which later steps LN runs itself.

tokens.v: A manually created warehousing order has no originating package, so the transaction type is set by hand and the order number comes from the Warehousing number group rather than from a sales or purchase order. For a same-company transfer LN copies the outbound and shipment activities and then the inbound and inspection activities onto this one order, so it carries both sides of the move.
